Chapter 9: Living with the Limits—Ethics, Action, and Attitude
So, now that we’ve explored the boundaries of language and the world, let’s talk about what really matters—how we actually live our lives. If the values that matter most can’t be fully put into words, how do they shape the way we act? Here’s where things get interesting: it’s not about following strict rules or memorizing a list of dos and don’ts. Instead, it’s all about the attitude we bring to each moment—how we live, how we act, and how we connect with others. Think about this: the most important ethical truths aren’t just facts to be debated. They’re ways of being that show up in every choice we make, every day.
Let’s highlight a few key points:
First, ethics isn’t about reciting what’s right or wrong—it’s about the way we live and act. Second, our deepest values show up in our actions, not just in what we say. Third, living well means accepting that language has its limits, and embracing what can only be shown through how we live. And finally, our attitude and approach matter so much more than any abstract theory. Here’s a helpful metaphor—think of ethics like a musical performance. The meaning of a piece of music isn’t in any one note, right? It’s in the way all the notes come together, the feeling that’s created. In the same way, the meaning of life doesn’t come from isolated statements. It comes from the harmony of our actions and our attitudes. When we live with awareness, humility, and care, we start to embody those values that words just can’t quite capture.
